map.center: Usamos el SECOND CONDITIONAL para situaciones imaginarias o poco probables y sus consecuencias.

nodes.title: ¿Qué es?
items: Algo imaginario o muy poco probable (ahora o en el futuro).
If I had a car, I'd drive to work. (Si tuviera coche, iría en coche.)

items: If I were taller, I'd play basketball.
(was se oye al hablar, pero were es lo correcto)

items: If I were you, I'd see a doctor. (Yo que tú, iría al médico.)

nodes.title: Negativas y preguntas
items: If I didn't work, I'd travel more.
I wouldn't go if I were you.

explain.es: El second conditional (segundo condicional) sirve para hablar de situaciones imaginarias, irreales o muy poco probables en el presente o en el futuro, y de sus consecuencias. Aunque el verbo va en pasado, ¡no hablamos del pasado! Aquí el pasado significa «lejos de la realidad». En español usamos imperfecto de subjuntivo + condicional: «Si tuviera dinero, viajaría».
explain.en: We use the second conditional for imaginary, unreal or unlikely situations in the present or future. The past form doesn't mean past time: it means «not real».

explain.title: 1 · La estructura
explain.es: En la parte del if usamos el past simple (had, lived, knew, spoke…). En el resultado usamos would + infinitivo sin to (forma corta: 'd). Traducción típica: si + tuviera / viviera → haría / iría.
explain.en: In the if-clause use the past simple. In the main clause use would + infinitive (short form 'd).

examples.en: If I had more free time, I'd learn to play the guitar.
examples.es: Si tuviera más tiempo libre, aprendería a tocar la guitarra.

examples.en: If we lived by the sea, we'd go surfing every weekend.
examples.es: Si viviéramos junto al mar, haríamos surf todos los fines de semana.

examples.en: If she spoke Chinese, she'd get that job.
examples.es: Si hablara chino, conseguiría ese trabajo.

explain.title: 2 · ¿Por qué pasado?
explain.es: Ojo: If I had a car no habla del pasado. Significa que ahora no tengo coche y me lo imagino. Compara: la realidad va en presente (I don't have a car); el «sueño», en pasado (If I had a car…).
explain.en: The past form shows the situation is not real now: I don't have a car → If I had a car, I'd drive to work.
formula: Realidad + I don't have a car

examples.en: I don't know her number. If I knew it, I'd call her.
examples.es: No sé su número. Si lo supiera, la llamaría.

examples.en: He isn't here. If he were here, he'd help us.
examples.es: No está aquí. Si estuviera, nos ayudaría.

examples.en: I can't drive. If I could drive, I'd take you to the airport.
examples.es: No sé conducir. Si supiera, te llevaría al aeropuerto.

explain.title: 3 · WERE con todas las personas
explain.es: Con el verbo to be, en el second conditional usamos were con todas las personas, también con I, he, she, it: if I were, if she were, if it were. Al hablar también se oye was (If I was…), pero were es la forma correcta en exámenes y textos cuidados.
explain.en: With be, use were for all persons (if I were, if she were). Was is common in speech, but were is safer in exams.

examples.en: If I were taller, I'd play basketball.
examples.es: Si fuera más alto, jugaría al baloncesto.

examples.en: If it weren't so expensive, I'd buy it.
examples.es: Si no fuera tan caro, lo compraría.

examples.en: If my sister were here, she'd know what to do.
examples.es: Si mi hermana estuviera aquí, sabría qué hacer.

explain.title: 4 · IF I WERE YOU: consejos
explain.es: If I were you, I'd… es la forma más típica de dar un consejo. Equivale a «yo que tú…» o «yo en tu lugar…». Puede ir al principio (con coma) o al final de la frase.
explain.en: If I were you, I'd… is a very common way to give advice (= Spanish «yo que tú»).
formula: *If I were you* + I'd / I wouldn't + infinitivo

examples.en: If I were you, I'd talk to your boss.
examples.es: Yo que tú, hablaría con tu jefe.

examples.en: I wouldn't post that photo if I were you.
examples.es: Yo en tu lugar no subiría esa foto.

examples.en: If I were you, I'd book the flights now. Prices are going up.
examples.es: Yo que tú, reservaría los vuelos ya. Los precios están subiendo.

explain.title: 5 · Negativas y preguntas
explain.es: Negativa en la condición: didn't + infinitivo (o weren't). Negativa en el resultado: wouldn't + infinitivo. Preguntas: (Wh-) + would + sujeto + infinitivo + if…? Respuestas cortas: Yes, I would. / No, I wouldn't.
explain.en: Negatives: didn't / weren't in the if-clause, wouldn't in the result. Questions: (Wh-) + would + subject + verb.

examples.en: If I didn't have to work, I'd come with you.
examples.es: Si no tuviera que trabajar, iría contigo.

examples.en: I wouldn't live in a big city if I had the choice.
examples.es: No viviría en una gran ciudad si pudiera elegir.

examples.en: What would you do if you lost your phone?

explain.title: 6 · COULD y MIGHT
explain.es: En el resultado podemos usar could (= podría) o might (= quizá…, a lo mejor…) en vez de would. Y en la condición, could significa «si pudiera / si supiera».
explain.en: In the result, use could (= would be able to) or might (= would perhaps). In the if-clause, could = were able to.

examples.en: If I had a car, I could visit my grandparents more often.
examples.es: Si tuviera coche, podría visitar a mis abuelos más a menudo.

examples.en: If you asked her nicely, she might say yes.
examples.es: Si se lo pidieras con amabilidad, a lo mejor te diría que sí.

examples.en: If I could live anywhere, I'd live in Canada.
examples.es: Si pudiera vivir en cualquier sitio, viviría en Canadá.

explain.title: Todo junto
head: Tipo · Type
Condición · If-clause
Resultado · Main clause
Traducción · Spanish
rows: Si tuviera dinero, viajaría por el mundo.
Si no tuviera exámenes, iría a la fiesta.
Si viviera en Madrid, no necesitaría coche.
Si fuera rico, me compraría una isla.
Si saliéramos ya, podríamos coger el tren.
explain.note: Truco de traducción: si + -ra / -se (tuviera, fuese) → past simple. Verbo en -ría (viajaría, iría) → would.

explain.title: ¿FIRST o SECOND?
explain.es: La gramática depende de lo probable que lo veas. First: es posible y realista. Second: es imaginario, imposible ahora o muy poco probable. ¡La misma idea puede ir con los dos!
explain.en: It depends on how likely you think it is. First = real possibility. Second = imaginary or unlikely.

cols.head: 🤞 FIRST · posible
items: If it rains, we'll stay in. (hay nubes)
If I see him, I'll tell him. (lo veo a menudo)

cols.head: 💭 SECOND · imaginario
items: If I won the lottery, I'd stop working. (casi imposible)
If it snowed in Seville, I'd be amazed. (muy raro)
If I were a bird, I'd fly home. (imposible)

explain.title: Pasados que vas a necesitar
head: Verbo · Verb
Pasado · Past
Ejemplo · Example
explain.note: Los verbos regulares solo añaden -ed: lived, worked, studied.

items.es: ¿Es imaginario, imposible o muy poco probable? → second. ¿Es posible y realista? → first.
items.en: Imaginary or unlikely → second. Realistic → first.

items.es: Condición: if + past simple (had, went, could…). Con be → were.
¿Quieres dar un consejo? Empieza con If I were you, I'd…
items.en: Advice → If I were you, I'd…

items.es: Revisa: ¿hay would en la parte del if? ¡Quítalo! ¿Empieza con if? Pon coma.
items.en: Check: no would after if; comma if you start with if.

explain.title: Truco: el pasado es «lejos»
explain.es: Imagina que el pasado en inglés es una forma de decir «lejos de la realidad». If I have → cerca, posible. If I had → lejos, imaginario. Y para traducir: -ra / -se del español (tuviera, fuese) = past simple; -ría (haría) = would.
explain.en: The past form = far from reality. If I have → possible. If I had → imaginary.

exercises.text_title: What would you do with a free year?
text: Last week we asked our followers a simple question: if you didn't have to work or study for a year, what would you do? Here are three of our favourite answers.
Hugo, 24: If I had a whole year free, I'd buy a van and travel around Europe. I'd sleep in the van, so I wouldn't need much money. If I got bored, I'd come home, but I don't think that would happen!

Nerea, 31: I'm a nurse and I love my job, but if I had a year off, I'd learn to cook properly. I'd do a course in Italy. If I were braver, I'd open my own restaurant afterwards, but I'm not sure I could do it.

Tom, 17: If I didn't have to study, I'd spend the year playing football. I'd train every day and maybe a big club would notice me. My mum says, «If I were you, I'd use the time to study.» Typical mum!

items.q: Hugo would travel around Europe by plane.
Hugo would need a lot of money.
items.why: He'd sleep in the van, so he wouldn't need much money.

items.q: Nerea doesn't like her job.
Tom's mum would use the year differently.
What would Nerea learn to do?
items.a: She'd learn to cook (properly).

items.q: Where would she do a course?
items.a: She'd do a course in Italy.

items.q: What would Nerea do if she were braver?
items.a: She'd open her own restaurant.

items.q: What would Tom do every day?
items.a: He'd train (play football) every day.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Imagina y escribe. Usa if + pasado y would / could.
exercises.en: Imagine and write. Use if + past and would / could.

items.q: Termina la frase: If I could have any job, …
items.a: Ej.: If I could have any job, I'd be a pilot.

items.q: Un amigo no duerme bien. Dale un consejo: If I were you, …
items.a: Ej.: If I were you, I wouldn't look at my phone in bed.

items.q: Escribe 2 frases: una first (posible) y una second (imaginaria).
items.a: Ej.: If it's sunny, I'll go to the beach. If I had a boat, I'd go sailing.

items.q: Escribe 2 preguntas What would you do if…? para un amigo.
items.a: Ej.: What would you do if you met your favourite singer? What would you do if you could fly?

checklist.es: Sé formar el second conditional: if + pasado, would + infinitivo.
checklist.en: I can form the second conditional.

checklist.es: Entiendo que aquí el pasado significa imaginario, no pasado.
checklist.en: I know the past form means unreal, not past.

checklist.es: Uso were con todas las personas: If I were…
checklist.en: I use were for all persons.

checklist.es: Sé dar consejos con If I were you, I'd…
checklist.en: I can give advice with If I were you.

checklist.es: Nunca pongo <s>would</s> en la parte del if.
checklist.en: I never use would after if.
I know the difference between first and second conditional.
